transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

Emptying the top container repeatedly will not clear this if water is backing up lower down. The most likely cause is a fluff blockage in the condenser/lower filter or condensate sump; after that, the likely parts are the condensate pump or its float/level switch. 1. Switch the dryer off and unplug it. Open the lower front flap, if fitted. Remove the condenser cassette or lower filter(s), following the markings, and clean off all fluff. Rinse only parts intended to be washable, then let them drip-dry before refitting.
2. Refit the water container firmly all the way home. Check it is not cracked and that its lid/float area is clean. Then run one normal drying programme and stay nearby. If the lower filter/condenser was blocked and it now runs normally, that was the cause. If it still stops with the container remaining empty after those areas are clear, water is likely not being lifted from the lower sump: the condensate pump, float switch, or an internal hose blockage needs checking. That normally means an engineer, as access involves dismantling the dryer.

Ok, I've reseated the container (it clicks in firmly) and cleaned the container's filter, which was pretty slimy. I also cleaned the condenser and fluff filters, but they were fairly clean already. I can't pull the dryer out as it's stacked on the washer, so what else can I check from the front?

Yes — there is one useful check you can do entirely from the front, but there is unlikely to be a user-serviceable reset or pump access there. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Open the lower front flap and use a torch to look only at the accessible area around/below the filters or condenser. Do not poke tools into any openings. If you can see standing water, very wet fluff, or sludge, that points to a blocked lower sump/drain path or a pump that is not lifting the water. 2. Put everything back, then run a short cycle with one damp towel and stay with it. When the warning returns, check whether the top container has collected any water. If it remains empty, despite the dryer having been running with damp laundry, the leading suspects are the condensate pump, its float/level switch, or an internal hose/sump blockage. The slimy container filter makes a sludge blockage plausible, but as the condenser and fluff filters were fairly clean and reseating the container made no difference, a pump or float fault is now more likely. Those parts are normally reached by dismantling the dryer, so with it stacked I would not try to move or strip it down. If you find water below, or the container stays empty on that test, book an engineer and describe it as: “Bosch condenser/heat-pump dryer stops on the water-container warning; tank is seated and empty; filters/condenser cleaned; possible condensate pump, float or sump blockage.”

I had a look with a torch and found a small cover near the condenser. Behind it was grey slimy water and fluff, so I wiped out what I could reach. I then ran it again and it went for about 60 minutes this time, but the empty container light came on again, and the container was still nearly empty.

That result points to the lower condensate system rather than the top water container. The grey slimy water and fluff show that the sump area is contaminated; wiping the accessible part has improved it, but after about an hour it is still not pumping enough water up to the container. Most likely, in order: a remaining blockage in the sump/drain path, fluff around or inside the condensate pump, or a sticking float/level switch. A failed pump is also possible, but the sludge means it should not be condemned until the sump and pump area have been properly cleaned. As the dryer is stacked and the remaining access requires dismantling, I would stop running it for now and book an appliance engineer. Ask them to inspect and clean the condensate sump, pump and associated hose, and test the float/level switch and condensate pump. Describe it as: “Bosch dryer stops on the water-container warning; container is seated but nearly empty; condenser and filters cleaned; grey sludge and water found behind the lower cover; it now runs for about an hour but then stops again.” This is usually a repairable drainage fault, not a reason by itself to replace the dryer.
